one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent fixated on simple one-dominant-token and exponential-decay parameterizations that are mathematically incapable of achieving KL_forward = KL_backward = 10.0 simultaneously, repeatedly saving noncompliant distributions and ultimately concluding incorrectly that the problem was infeasible.
t_err_evidence: Step 5 introduces the two-parameter model (one dominant token p1, rest uniform) as the core framework via solve_kl_analytical.py. This parameterization is structurally unable to achieve KL_forward = KL_backward = 10.0 simultaneously because the two KL divergences move monotonically and asymmetrically as p1 varies; no single crossing point yields both at 10.0. The agent adopts this false premise and all subsequent scripts are variants of the same flawed model family (exponential decay, power law, multi-special-token).
t_commit_evidence: Step 19 is where the agent issues a premature completion claim ('Task completed. Distribution saved to /app/dist.npy with KL divergences close to target value of 10.0') despite errors of ~0.25 each. After this, the agent's actual behavior shifts to a resigned cycle of trying marginally different variants of the same flawed model family, then culminates in declaring infeasibility (steps 27-30) without ever pivoting to a proper constrained optimization or analytical approach capable of achieving equal KL values at 10.0.
t_surface_evidence: Step 10 first reveals the failure explicitly: the script prints 'KL_f error=1.743205, KL_b error=5.394947' and '⚠ Close but not perfect' while saving a noncompliant /app/dist.npy, making the failure observable in terminal output.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumes without verification that a one-dominant-token distribution (step 5) or its variants (exponential decay, power law) is expressive enough to satisfy KL_forward = KL_backward = 10.0. This is a false premise: for a distribution with a single dominant mass plus a uniform tail, KL(P||U) and KL(U||P) are both monotone functions of the dominant probability but diverge in opposite directions, making equality at a specific high value structurally impossible in this model family. The agent never analyzes this structural constraint and instead iterates on the same family with more parameters, mistakenly attributing failure to numerical optimization difficulty rather than model insufficiency.
forewarning_evidence: Step 6 output shows the two-parameter model yields alpha=3.85 (>1, clearly invalid as a probability) and KL_f=11.92 vs KL_b=9.998 — the two KLs are on opposite sides of the target in a structurally asymmetric way, signaling the model family cannot achieve equality. Step 3 also shows the initial optimization was killed mid-run (C-c in step 4) because it was too slow, and the initial KL values (KL_f=9.30, KL_b=2.03) showed a large gap between the two divergences, foreshadowing the structural difficulty.
